lessons.situation: A contractor's quote for follow-on plumbing works was sent to the landlord, the request was held awaiting their reply, and the landlord has now replied approving the quote.
lessons.action: Read the landlord's reply to confirm it is a clear approval. Attach the approved quote to the job record, log that the landlord approved it, and move the task on to the next stage. No further reply to the landlord is needed, so release the hold and return the request to auto mode. Send the tenant a short email saying the maintenance provider will contact them to schedule the approved work, and remind them to tell the provider about any pets.
lessons.rationale: A clear landlord approval needs no further response, so recording it, keeping the tenant informed and handing the job back to automation lets the contractor be booked without delay.

lessons.situation: A landlord replied to a repair request saying they will sort the issue themselves with their own contractor, so the agency no longer needs to arrange works but still needs to know when the job is done.
lessons.action: Read the landlord's reply to check whether it needs a response; if it only confirms they will handle the repair, send no further reply. Put the request on hold with the reason 'Waiting for Landlord' and a comment saying it is held awaiting the landlord's contractor to complete. If the tenant or landlord later gives no update, chase the landlord politely for progress and keep the hold in place until the contractor reports completion.
lessons.rationale: When the landlord takes ownership of the repair, the agency's role changes from instructing works to monitoring them, so the request must stay paused rather than return to auto mode, and the landlord must be chased so the job does not stall unnoticed.

lessons.situation: After a landlord received a quote for check-out works on a vacant property, they replied asking for a second subcontractor to quote for comparison, and the system had flagged the task for the agent to decide whether a response was needed or to return it to auto mode.
lessons.action: Read the landlord's reply and treat a request for a comparison quote as a prompt for manual action rather than returning the job to auto mode. Note the landlord's request, assign a new provider to obtain the second estimate, and keep the job on hold until that quote arrives. If the property shows as not tenanted and the job is auto-paused, review it manually and do not resume automation until the quote comparison is resolved.
lessons.rationale: A landlord asking for an alternative quote is a decision point that automation cannot handle, so a human must arrange the extra provider and keep control of the job until the landlord can compare quotes and approve.

lessons.situation: A tenant reported a door that has become hard to shut, and the landlord replied with a known workaround from past experience and proposed deferring any contractor visit.
lessons.action: Relay the landlord's workaround to the tenant by phone and ask them to try it before any contractor is booked. If it works, tell the landlord you are closing the request unless the tenant reports the problem again, and ask the tenant to come back if it recurs. Don't send a formal response chasing approval or book a contractor, and return the request to auto mode or close it.
lessons.rationale: When the landlord supplies a workable fix for a non-urgent, recurring fault and the tenant confirms it works, a contractor visit is unnecessary. Closing with a clear route to reopen keeps costs down while protecting the tenant.

lessons.situation: A repair request was on hold awaiting the landlord's choice of contractor, and the landlord has replied naming the contractor they want to use for the job.
lessons.action: Treat the landlord's reply as approval and as the contractor choice, so no further response to the landlord is needed. Assign the named contractor as the maintenance provider and return the request to auto mode. Then notify the tenant that the contractor will be in touch, and send the contractor the job details so they can arrange access or quote if needed.
lessons.rationale: The landlord's reply already answers the open question of who should attend, so replying again would only add noise. Assigning the provider and notifying both parties moves the job forward.
